content.text:
The file was created in commit `b463960` with a syntactically-broken anonymous class body — the `performHighlight` method declaration was accidentally omitted, leaving a bare `if` block directly inside the class body (which wouldn't even compile as written, or if it compiled due to some quirk, it meant the highlight-suppression logic was never actually wired into an overridden method). Commit `dc4ddf0` fixes this by adding back the `protected void performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e) {` method signature.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b4639602a22a16c7bd671ffd1cc2d1dafabd501d

## Reasoning
(1) I searched the git history for `CustomPieChart.java` using `git log --follow`, which showed only two commits ever touched this file: `b463960` (file creation) and `dc4ddf0` (the given bug-fix). Since there's no earlier history, the bug must have been introduced when the file was created.

(2) In `b463960`, the anonymous `PieRadarChartTouchListener` subclass body contains a bare `if (h != null && !h.equalTo(mLastHighlighted)) { ... }` block with no enclosing method — the `protected void performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e) {` declaration is missing. The fix commit `dc4ddf0` restores exactly this missing method signature and its closing brace, without changing any other logic (aside from removing now-unused imports `View`, `ChartTouchListener`, `OnChartGestureListener` that were only needed for the override annotation context).

(3) The diff of `dc4ddf0` is a pure structural fix — same field references (`h`, `mLastHighlighted`, `mChart`), same logic — just re-adding the method wrapper that makes the code override `performHighlight` correctly. This strongly indicates the original commit `b463960` had a copy-paste/omission error when authoring the anonymous class, and since it's the sole commit that created this file, it is the bug-introducing commit with high confidence.
